thread:
Alex: heads-up — received a SEV ticket from Support: multiple customers reporting p95/p99 spikes on dedicated pools (EU).

Maria: details? which pool, metrics?

Alex: customer reports started ~08:10 UTC, p95 went from ~120ms to ~900ms, p99 to ~2.1s. They attached traces showing first-token delay. Support says errors are rare, mostly latency.

Sanjay: opened dashboards — I see a large jump in request queue length for pool `dedicated-eu-west-1-pool-23` starting 08:09. GPU utilization pinned at 98-100% across 12 nodes. Scale-up events show new nodes requested at 08:11 but not ready until 08:17. avg cold GPU init ~90s, plus kube scheduling delays.

Kira (oncall): is this the new model rollout we launched yesterday?

Maria: yes — model `redwood-v2-compact:2026-03-10` was added to that pool and we enabled traffic split 20% last night. Could be throughput mismatch.

Leah: I pulled logs from the autoscaler. Looks like scaling was triggered but rate-limited by our per-region pod quota and the cloud account hit async provisioning backoff. Autoscaler backoff shows repeated 429s from cloud API between 08:12-08:14.

Alex: so two issues: pool saturated by traffic + cloud API rate-limit caused scale-up lag + cold-start overhead -> p95/p99 spikes. Any immediate mitigations?

Sanjay: short-term: 1) divert traffic away from the pool (route new requests to `dedicated-eu-west-1-pool-21` and `-22`) 2) bump pool size manually if quota allows 3) enable burst capacity for this customer. I can flip routing for the affected customer id if approved.

Maria: can we set a circuit-breaker to reduce concurrent model instances per connection? Some requests are long, causing KV cache retention and blocking slots.

Leah: also we should temporarily reduce cooldown and disable aggressive backoff so autoscaler retries faster — but careful, cloud 429s might persist.

Kira (oncall): DeployBot: post status?

DeployBot: Incident acknowledged, runbook: dedicated-pool-latency. Incident ID INC-20260310-17825. Triage channel created.

Alex: Sanjay, do the routing divert. Leah, can you request a soft quota increase from cloud ops? Maria, rollback the traffic split for that model to 0% on the pool.

Sanjay: On it. Routing change applied at 08:30 UTC for the customer (ID cust-1347). Verified 5xx remain low. Observability: p95 for that customer's requests dropped to ~150ms after divert. Other customers still affected while we act.

Leah: opened cloud support ticket, requested temporary boost of 8 GPUs for eu-west region. ETA unknown. Also disabling autoscaler aggressive backoff now (08:33).

Maria: rollback of model traffic completed at 08:34. Rolling window shows aggregate p95 for pool down from 920ms to ~310ms but p99 still near 1.6s.

Alex: what's the story on cold starts? Any ways to reduce first-token latency for cold GPUs?

Sanjay: two levers: 1) pre-warm a small standby set with the common model variants loaded (warm pool), 2) reduce model init cost by switching to a smaller quantized checkpoint for warmups. Warm pool requires config change and extra reserved capacity.

Leah: ops reply: soft quota increase approved +5 GPUs immediate, additional +3 pending manual review. Provisioning started at 08:40, nodes reported ready at 08:48. Scale-up lag improved for subsequent events.

Kira (oncall): any repro steps we can give Support to collect traces for other customers?

Maria: yes — ask Support to collect full trace for these fields: request id, model tag, pool id, start_time, time to first token, total tokens, gpu_node_id. Also capture the pool's `queue_depth` and `kv_cache_hit` boolean.

Alex: also useful: PromQL snippets for them to copy: `sum(rate(inference_requests[1m])) by (pool)`, `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le) )`, and `sum(kube_node_status_capacity_gpu)` to correlate.

Sanjay: note: during the incident we saw repeated cold-starts because traffic was bursty — multiple new models were requested concurrently causing many processes to initialize and evict caches. We should add a guard: disallow >N model init requests per pool per minute.

Leah: action item list so far:
- Sanjay: keep traffic diverted for cust-1347 until pool stable, add guard to routing (in-progress)
- Maria: revert model rollout globally for `redwood-v2-compact` until we verify perf (done for this pool, consider global pause)
- Leah: follow up on cloud quota + confirm node ready times (cloud ticket #CL-4491)
- Alex: schedule postmortem with eng-runtime and product (tomorrow 11:00 UTC)

Maria: FYI — I ran a quick `strace`-style sampling on an affected worker: model init does two expensive ops: 1) mmap large quantized weights (~3.2GB read spikes) 2) JIT kernel compile step (~40s in worst case). If we can cache the compiled kernels on local disk across restarts we'll shave a ton off cold start.

Sanjay: suggestion: add a pre-pull hook for new nodes that downloads model artifacts and triggers kernel compile before marking node ready. Implementation: small init job that pulls `/models/redwood-v2-compact/*` and runs `compile_kernels.sh`.

Alex: long-term roadmap items: warm pool config, pre-pull on node startup, kernel cache persist across instance life, autoscaler smarter quotas (consider cloud API 429 handling), and rollout throttles per pool. We'll track in ENGRT-624.

Kira (oncall): current status?

Sanjay: as of 08:55 UTC, affected pool p95 ~220ms, p99 ~900ms. Cloud nodes stabilized. No new alerts in last 10m. Still monitoring.

Leah: will keep cloud ticket open until +3 GPUs provisioned.

Alex: thanks all. I'll start the incident notes and invite eng-runtime/product to the postmortem. If anyone finds a smoking gun log or repro, drop it here.

Maria: one more note — Support asked for a short customer-facing blurb. Draft: "We experienced temporary latency degradations due to unexpected capacity saturation and a downstream cloud provisioning delay. Mitigations applied and we are implementing warm-pools and pre-warm measures to prevent recurrence." Thoughts?

Alex: good. Add an apology and timeline. Send once PM signs off.

DeployBot: Incident INC-20260310-17825 marked RESOLVED at 09:12 UTC (status: mitigated).

Leah: closing loop with cloud: +3 GPUs approved at 09:05 and are active.

Sanjay: assigning ENGRT-624 and ENGOPS-191 for the follow-ups.

Alex: end thread — great work.
